title: Understanding cloud security solutions
content:
## Overview

Public cloud environments introduce unique security challenges. According to the 2023 Cloud Security Report conducted by Cybersecurity Insiders and sponsored by Fortinet, more than 51% of surveyed cybersecurity professionals consider misconfigurations of the public cloud the number one threat. Malware, insecure interfaces and APIs, and exfiltration of sensitive data are also commonly reported threats. The top challenges of the public cloud are security responsibility, selecting the right cloud architecture, and achieving regulatory compliance.

![Understanding cloud security solutions](diagram:0)

## Fortinet Multicloud Security

As the leader in multicloud security, Fortinet gives organizations the confidence to deploy any application in any cloud. Fortinet solutions provide broad protection across the entire digital attack surface, both on-premises and in public clouds such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Native integration with each of the major cloud providers enables automated, centralized management across all clouds uniformly and seamlessly, delivering unified visibility, control, and policy management that supports risk management and compliance requirements.

Fortinet offers three solution categories for securing the cloud:

- **Secure connectivity** (Infrastructure-as-a-Service / IaaS): Provides network-level security, VPN, and connectivity features for cloud workloads.
- **Application security**: Protects cloud-hosted applications, including web application firewall (WAF) capabilities.
- **Visibility and control**: Enables monitoring and governance across cloud environments.

For SaaS applications, Fortinet can provide only visibility and control — creating an IPsec tunnel or WAF to a SaaS application like Dropbox is not possible.

## Key Capabilities

Fortinet cloud security is not a replacement for existing cloud vendor security but an added layer that provides greater control, visibility, and optimized protection beyond native options. The three pillars of this approach are:

- **Management and automation**: Fortinet offers a single-pane-of-glass solution that enables consistent management of protection services natively integrated into cloud infrastructure. This approach automates management through standard web-based APIs and supports predefined automation recipes. By extending this automation framework across multiple cloud environments, customers can embed security services into DevOps-driven application lifecycles.

- **Broad protection**: By offering the broadest set of security products both in and out of the cloud, Fortinet enables customers to consistently build highly secure infrastructures, regardless of deployment mode, workflow complexity, or degree of scale. Native integration allows Fortinet to deliver multiple security products across and between cloud environments offered by every major cloud service provider.

- **Native integration**: Integration seamlessly extends consistent security across every major cloud platform, enabling organizations to define security uniformly across their multicloud and on-premises deployments. Native integration also allows security products to consume cloud services natively, delivering faster, more seamless protection and response.

title: Understanding FortiGate VM and FortiGate CNF
content:
## Overview

Fortinet provides two primary solutions for securing cloud environments: **FortiGate VM** — a full-featured virtual machine — and **FortiGate CNF** (Cloud-Native Firewall), a Firewall-as-a-Service (FWaaS). Selecting the right solution depends on your organization's requirements for features, scalability, and operational overhead.

![Understanding FortiGate VM and FortiGate CNF](diagram:0)

## FortiGate VM

FortiGate VM is a powerful virtual instance offering advanced security, VPN, SD-WAN, and routing features. Its capabilities enable complex configurations and granular control. For example, FortiGate VM for AWS delivers critical features not included by default in AWS native services, such as VPN, SD-WAN, and dynamic routing. FortiGate also supports additional IPsec topologies such as full mesh and partial mesh.

The main licensing models are:

- **Pay-as-you-go (PAYG)**: Billed based on consumption through the cloud marketplace.
- **Bring your own license (BYOL)**: Customer provides an existing Fortinet license.
- **FortiFlex**: A prepaid enterprise license for Fortinet VM use, trackable through the FortiCloud portal using a point-based system.

FortiGate VM for public cloud delivers complete content and network protection by combining stateful inspection with NGFW features:

- **Application control** identifies thousands of applications, including cloud applications, for deep inspection of network traffic.
- **FortiGuard Labs** provides continuous threat intelligence that protects against known exploits and malware.
- **IPS** performs both signature-based and anomaly-based detection against current and emerging network-level threats.
- **Sandboxing integration** protects against unknown attacks using dynamic analysis and provides automated mitigation.
- **APIs for automation** enable integration with cloud and SDN extensions, such as AWS GuardDuty threat intelligence feeds for automated incident response.

A simple FortiGate VM deployment in the cloud places the VM in a protected subnet with internal and external interfaces, with internet traffic inspected through FortiGate.

## FortiGate CNF

Manually deploying and managing FortiGate devices can be complex and time-consuming. FortiGate CNF is a FWaaS that reduces network security operations workloads — enterprises no longer need to configure, provision, or maintain firewall software infrastructure. CNF leverages FortiOS to provide consistent availability, scalability, and ease-of-use.

Key use cases for FortiGate CNF include:

- Protecting cloud workloads from threats associated with outbound communication by blocking malicious IP communication and enforcing geographical fences.
- Securing lateral (east-west) traffic within cloud networks using dynamic objects.
- Protecting assets hosted in the cloud from inbound threats.

Enterprise benefits of FortiGate CNF:

- **Enterprise-grade protection**: Supports NGFW security inspection including geo-IP blocking, advanced filtering, and threat protection.
- **Zero operations overhead**: A single FortiGate CNF instance secures an entire AWS or Azure region, protecting multiple accounts, subnets, VPCs, and availability zones.
- **Simplified management**: Use the FortiGate CNF console or FortiManager for hybrid deployments. Integrates with AWS Firewall Manager to streamline security workflows.
- **Lower costs**: No security software infrastructure to build, deploy, or operate. Aggregating security into a single CNF instance avoids per-network charges. Uses AWS Graviton instances for better price performance.

## FortiGate CNF vs FortiGate VM

FortiGate CNF is the preferred choice when NGFW functionality, ease of management, and scalability are the primary requirements. Choose FortiGate VM when you need additional features such as VPN, SD-WAN, or NAT functionality.

FortiGate CNF uses the **AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)** to forward traffic for inspection. The GWLB deploys a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (GWLBe) referenced in AWS route tables, routing traffic through FortiGate CNF before reaching the internet gateway. In Azure, CNF connects a GWLB to an existing server load balancer or public IP, with traffic forwarded to FortiGate CNF for policy enforcement and then passed through Azure NAT Gateway.

Setting up FortiGate CNF requires associating your AWS or Azure account, creating a CNF instance (which may take up to ten minutes), and deploying a load balancer endpoint in your cloud accounts. A FortiGate CNF instance is dedicated to one customer but can connect to multiple VPCs, accounts, and availability zones.

> **Key terms:** IPS performs anomaly-based detection, alerting users to traffic matching attack behavior profiles.

> **Key terms:** FortiGate CNF protects against threats like malware downloads, data exfiltration, C&C communication, cryptomining, and compliance violations.

> **Key terms:** If traffic is not blocked, it is sent back to the GWLBe it was received from and then passes out through the internet gateway.

title: FortiSASE
content:
## Overview

The current network infrastructure — relying on corporate VPNs and data centers for access — combined with the growing use of hybrid work models and distributed applications, presents significant security challenges. Inconsistent security policies, lack of visibility into SaaS traffic, and VPN-related performance and security risks drive the need for a modern approach: **Secure Access Service Edge (SASE)**.

![FortiSASE](diagram:0)

## Key Challenges Driving SASE Adoption

Organizations face three major challenges with traditional network security approaches:

- **Inconsistent security**: Remote workers outside the corporate network are considered "untrusted" and must use a VPN, while branch office employees are deemed "trusted" and connect directly. Remote internet access from endpoints like BYOD devices isn't protected by the same corporate policies as office access, creating a gap that allows malware to enter and potentially spread to the corporate network.
- **Lack of visibility and control**: When securing data in SaaS applications, corporate infrastructures and data centers lack visibility into remotely accessed SaaS traffic, creating a blind spot in the security framework.
- **Performance issues**: Routing all user traffic through a VPN to access the internet and SaaS applications can degrade performance. VPNs also pose security risks by granting broad network access, allowing malware to infiltrate and spread.

## SASE Architecture

SASE provides hybrid and remote workers with secure access to corporate applications, data, and services so they can work from anywhere, no matter where the resources are located. SASE secures hybrid work by converging cloud-delivered security services with advanced networking capabilities.

SASE is built on a **zero-trust security posture**, emphasizing the principle of "never trust, always verify." SASE is composed of two parts:

- **SD-WAN**: On-premises security and networking for branch offices.
- **Security Service Edge (SSE)**: Cloud-delivered security for remote worker security and visibility.

SSE includes essential services:

- **Secure web gateway (SWG)** and **Firewall-as-a-Service (FWaaS)** to protect users and devices from web-based threats.
- **Zero trust network access (ZTNA)** that delivers secure, explicit, identity-based access.
- **Cloud access security broker (CASB)** that ensures secure access to SaaS applications and protects sensitive data.

## FortiSASE Solution

FortiSASE is the Fortinet unified SASE approach that empowers organizations to consistently apply enterprise-grade security and superior user experience across all edges, converging networking and security across a unified OS and agent. Both FortiSASE (for SSE) and secure SD-WAN are built on the unified foundation of **FortiOS**.

FortiSASE extends FortiGuard security services across thin edge, secure edge, and remote users. Its main objectives are:

- Achieve secure internet access for off-net endpoints connecting to a cloud-delivered security service located between the user and the internet.
- Reduce latency by connecting off-net endpoints to the closest **point of presence (POP)**.
- Scale dynamically to meet traffic demands and reduce congestion with geographically distributed POPs.
- Enforce a zero-trust model for protected network access.

FortiSASE supports three primary use cases:

- **SIA (Secure Internet Access)**: Enables secure web browsing for remote users, protecting against known and unknown threats.
- **SPA (Secure Private Access)**: Enables explicit application access under zero-trust or with SD-WAN integration.
- **SSA (Secure SaaS Access)**: Addresses shadow IT visibility and safeguards data loss prevention.

Additional FortiSASE capabilities include ZTNA for agentless devices, **FortiCASB** for deep SaaS inspection with inline and out-of-band modes, **DLP** (data loss prevention) to protect organizational data at rest and in motion, **digital experience monitoring (DEM)** for troubleshooting connectivity, and **remote browser isolation (RBI)** for safely rendering web content in a remote container.

> **Key terms:** RBI (Remote Browser Isolation) isolates browser sessions for specific websites or categories within a secure environment, safely rendering content in a remote container.

> **Key terms:** FortiSASE supports SAML, RADIUS, and LDAP for SSO and user authentication.

title: Secure access service edge (SASE) use cases
content:
## Overview

FortiSASE delivers several deployment use cases to address the diverse security needs of modern organizations. These use cases — **Secure Internet Access (SIA)**, **Secure Private Access (SPA)**, and **Secure SaaS Access (SSA)** — each cover distinct scenarios for protecting users, applications, and data wherever they are located.

![Secure access service edge (SASE) use cases](diagram:0)

## Secure Internet Access (SIA)

SIA is one of the FortiSASE use cases. The comprehensive FWaaS and SWG capabilities secure managed and unmanaged devices by supporting agent and agentless approaches. Natively integrated FortiGuard AI-Powered Security Services protect content and users from ransomware and other sophisticated attacks. SIA extends an organization's security perimeter to remote users by enforcing common security policies for IPS, application control, web filtering, DNS filtering, antimalware, sandboxing, antibotnet, and command-and-control (C&C) protection.

FortiSASE SIA supports multiple deployment modes:

- **Agent-based**: FortiClient connects to FortiSASE using a secure VPN tunnel (IPsec by default). FortiSASE acts as a firewall between the endpoint and the internet. The VPN policy enforces web filtering, application control, and ZTNA compliance checks.
- **Agentless**: FortiSASE acts as a SWG and distributes a proxy auto-configuration (PAC) file. SWG secures only web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) by acting as an explicit web proxy. All other non-web traffic bypasses FortiSASE. This mode is recommended for unmanaged endpoints like contractors or temporary employees.
- **Thin edge (LAN extension)**: FortiExtender or FortiGate is deployed at a remote location, forms an IPsec tunnel to FortiSASE, and a VXLAN is established over the tunnel to create a layer 2 network. FortiSASE inspects traffic for users connected to the LAN extension.
- **Branch access**: Connects branch offices through a third-party router or FortiGate.

FortiSASE redirects the internet traffic of remote users to the closest FortiSASE POP using geolocation selection, reducing latency. FortiSASE also provides native support for full SSL inspection at no additional cost.

## Secure Private Access (SPA)

FortiSASE SPA offers two options for accessing private applications:

- **Direct application access without traversing FortiSASE POPs**: Ideal for latency-sensitive applications. ZTNA capabilities are enforced for user traffic along this path, ensuring continuous verification. Traffic is not inspected inline since it bypasses FortiSASE POPs.
- **Application access through FortiSASE POPs for inline inspection**: Traffic is routed through FortiSASE POPs before reaching private applications. This provides inline security inspection for robust threat protection, plus SD-WAN benefits for optimizing traffic flow between the POP and the SD-WAN hub or FortiGate at the datacenter.

Both options support ZTNA, and user traffic undergoes continuous posture verification checking identity and device posture in near real time, creating a dynamic security model.

Integrating SD-WAN with FortiSASE creates a powerful solution: SD-WAN optimizes traffic routing based on real-time network conditions, while FortiSASE provides zero-trust security including real-time threat inspection, SSL inspection, CASB, and FWaaS. Critical applications can be given higher priority while less essential traffic is handled with lower urgency, optimizing bandwidth use.

## Secure SaaS Access (SSA) and CASB

Given the rapid increase in SaaS adoption, organizations struggle with shadow IT challenges and data exfiltration. FortiSASE includes **dual-mode CASB** with both inline and out-of-band support:

- **Inline CASB**: Detects data in motion as it passes through to the cloud application from the endpoint device. Uses IPS protocol decoders to analyze network traffic and detect application traffic even if it uses nonstandard ports or protocols. Web filter with inline CASB restricts tenant access to control SaaS application behavior by customizing HTTP headers for FortiSASE outgoing traffic.
- **Out-of-band CASB**: Uses an API to connect to the cloud application and scans data at rest — data already uploaded to the SaaS application. Access to the FortiCASB portal is included with per-user and per-endpoint FortiSASE licensing, and is configured independently of FortiSASE configurations.

FortiSASE also uses **DLP (data loss prevention)** to prevent sensitive data from leaving or entering the network by defining sensitive data patterns, scanning traffic for those patterns, and allowing, blocking, or logging when traffic matches.

FortiSASE supports multiple authentication methods including local database, RADIUS, LDAP, and SAML for SSO. Identity providers (IdP) are configured through the User Onboarding SSO page, enabling SSO to reduce password fatigue and improve user experience.
